atoms.span: The Electronic Literature Lab (ELL) is a media archaeology research facility
directed by Dr. Dene Grigar at
A dedicated space where scholars and visitors can access historical media running on original vintage hardware.
Maintains over 80 vintage Macintosh computers and PCs (dating back to 1977) along with a library of thousands of digital literary works
To archive, restore, conserve, and present born-digital art, literature, and video games from 1977 to the present.

mt: 'ELECTRONIC LITERATURE LAB' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE LAB AT ITS GRAIN FROM A SITE THE CENSUS DID NOT SAVE; ITS COUNTS LARGER THAN THE SAVED PAGE'S; ONE AUTHOR NAMED, IN A ROOM'S NAME
d: THE LAB, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The Electronic Literature Lab (ELL) is a media archaeology research facility founded in 2011 and directed by Dr. Dene Grigar at Washington State University Vancouver.' Mission (archive, restore, conserve and present 'born-digital art, literature, and video games from 1977 to the present'); collection ('over 80 vintage Macintosh computers and PCs', 'a library of thousands of digital literary works and retro video games'); archival center for the ELO and manager of The NEXT; four rooms (the Marjorie C. Luesebrink Reading Room, the Archives Room, the Restoration Room, the Studio); address, phone, electronicliteraturelab.org. Four cards: electronicliteraturelab.org, Washington State University, Wikipedia, Instagram.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the lab, the Overview gives its founding, director, mission, holdings, rooms and contact details, mostly from the lab's own site.
findings: THE COUNTS. 'over 80 vintage Macintosh computers and PCs (dating back to 1977)' and 'a library of thousands of digital literary works'. The page the census saved (Washington State University): 'ELL contains 61 vintage Macintosh computers and PCs, dating back from 1977 and a library of 200 electronic literary works.' That page's latest date is its list of '2021 Undergraduate Researchers'; the composition's first and most-cited card is electronicliteraturelab.org, which the census did not save. The census row's counts are the 2021-era page's.

THE DATE. 'founded in 2011'. The census row gives no founding date. The NEXT's Wikipedia article, saved for the census, says 'The lab opened officially in 2011', and the composition's Wikipedia card, an article on the lab itself, gives 'founded 2011 by Dene Grigar'.

THE LAB AND THE MUSEUM. 'Serves as the primary archiving center for the Electronic Literature Organization and manages The NEXT digital museum, library, and preservation space.' The NEXT's home page: 'managed by the Electronic Literature Lab'; Wikipedia: 'Physical artifacts are held at the Electronic Literature Lab'. The ELO archiving role is on no saved source.

ONE AUTHOR, IN A ROOM'S NAME. The census row: 'the saved page names a library of 200 electronic literary works and lists none of their authors'. The composition names one, 'Marjorie C. Luesebrink Reading Room', under the civil name; The NEXT's Wikipedia account holds 27 of her works 'under the pen name M.D. Coverley'. The one work the composition names is a game ('Amnesia from 1986'), given without its author.
analysis: The lab composed at its grain from its own newer site, with counts that exceed the 2021-era page the census rests on. Whose works the library holds, and under what names, is not carried; the one author named stands in the name of a room.
per_note: Dene Grigar and WSU Vancouver named; the lab's two sites, Wikipedia and Instagram carded.
